forecaster_note: No Surfline forecaster paragraph was published for the Northern Beaches this refresh - the read below comes straight off Surfline's model data (wave, wind, rating, tide and weather endpoints, pulled 6:10am AEST). Saturday sits at 1-2ft with only 9-19 kJ of energy and a light W offshore. Overnight a S groundswell fills in hard: 5.7ft @ 9s from 182 deg plus a 16-18s long-period pulse, peaking at 508 kJ around 6am Sunday, with W/WNW offshore under 5 kph until mid-morning before a NE onshore takes over from midday. - Surf Guru read of Surfline model data

wind.summary: Light W offshore 9-12 kph through the morning, easing and swinging S/SE cross-shore from about 3pm.

shark.summary: No detections at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly. Nearest Northern Beaches report: a drone-spotted shark at Newport Beach Fri 12:23pm (~18h ago, water evacuated). Feed is live - 8 detections statewide in the last 24h.

days.label: Today
days.note: Flat-ish and glassy. Knee-to-thigh NE windswell, only 9-19 kJ of energy, light W offshore all morning. Ride something with volume or save your energy - the real swell fills in overnight and Sunday dawn is the session of the weekend.

dee-why.window: 10am–12pm on the pushing tide off the 8:46am low. Small but clean - Point is soft, the beachie has slightly more push.

tip.label: Board call
tip.text: 19 kJ is nothing - go up in volume. Groveller or a log, not the Inferno 72. NE windswell at 6s means short, fast walls: keep your feet forward and generate your own speed.

long-reef.window: Best around the 4:02pm high if you want a bit more water - the bank needs size and it isn't getting any today.

tip.label: Skip note
tip.text: Long Reef needs swell to switch on. At 6s NE windswell it's the weakest of the four. Leave it for tomorrow.

curl-curl.window: Mid-morning 9am–12pm while the W offshore holds. South corner will have the most shape.

tip.label: Frontside note
tip.text: South Curly bank throws a few rights on a NE swell - frontside for you. Small but rippable on a wide-tailed board.

manly.window: Anytime this morning - it's a paddle-fitness session, not a scoring one.

tip.label: Backside note
tip.text: North Steyne lefts are the go if you want backside reps, but at knee-high it's more of a warm-up than a surf.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The one. A solid S groundswell lands overnight - 5.7ft @ 9s from 182 deg with a 16-18s long-period pulse underneath it, and energy spikes to 508 kJ at first light. Light W/WNW offshore until roughly 10am, then a NE onshore ruins it from midday. Be in the water by 6:30am.

dee-why.window: Dawn to 10am. Wind is only 4–5 kph W/WNW - as clean as it gets. NE swings onshore around midday and it's over.
alerts: Swell is dead S (182 deg) - it wraps badly into Dee Why. The Point will hold shape better than the beachie; expect the bay to be smaller than the open beaches.

long-reef.window: 6:30–10am, best of the four. Straight S swell angle is exactly what Long Reef wants - dawn patrol here.
alerts: Biggest of the four - 4–6ft with a 16s underlying pulse. Expect solid sets and a working rip.

curl-curl.window: 6:30–10am. Punchy and well-exposed to the S angle - the size you actually like.
alerts: Rating drops to fair by midday as the NE gets in. Front half of the morning only.

manly.window: Early only. The headland blocks most of the S angle - smallest and softest option, good if the others look too heavy.
alerts: Shadowed by the S direction - roughly half the size of Long Reef.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is a write-off for size, Sunday is the payday. If you only surf once this weekend, make it Sunday between 6:30 and 10am at Long Reef or Curl Curl. Numbers below are Sunday's - the weekend's best window.

dee-why.window: Sun 6:30–10am. Dead-S angle limits it - Point over beachie.

curl-curl.window: Sun 6:30–10am. Punchy 4–5ft with shape - your favourite window.

manly.window: Sun early. Fallback if the S swell looks too much.
